About our school

An education built on care, character and steady progress

At The Saif School System, we believe every child learns best when they feel known, encouraged and challenged in the right measure.

Our teachers build strong foundations in language, mathematics and the sciences, and give equal weight to good manners, curiosity and independent thinking. Lessons are structured, classrooms are calm, and children are taught to take pride in careful work.

We see parents as partners. Families can expect open communication, honest feedback and a school that listens.

  • Integrity

    Honesty and fairness in work, in play and in how we treat one another.

  • Respect

    Courtesy towards teachers, classmates, families and the wider community.

  • Curiosity

    Asking questions, reading widely and enjoying the effort of finding out.

  • Responsibility

    Taking ownership of learning, conduct and the shared spaces of our school.

Academics

A clear path from the first day of school

Each stage builds on the one before it, so children move forward with secure knowledge and growing independence.

Sample programme outline, to be confirmed by the school

Stage one

Early Years

A gentle, joyful start where young children learn through play, stories, song and hands-on discovery.

The Early Years programme helps children settle happily into school life. Days follow a predictable rhythm of circle time, guided activities, outdoor play and rest, so that young learners feel secure and ready to explore.

Areas of focus

  • Spoken language, listening and early phonics in English and Urdu
  • Number sense through counting, sorting and pattern games
  • Fine and gross motor skills through art, building and movement
  • Sharing, taking turns and looking after belongings

How children learn

Teachers plan purposeful play and short, focused activities in small groups, and keep parents informed about how their child is settling and progressing.

Sample outline. Age ranges, class names and timings will be confirmed by the school.

Stage two

Primary School

Strong foundations in reading, writing and mathematics, taught with patience, structure and encouragement.

In the primary years, children become fluent readers, confident writers and secure mathematicians. Teachers introduce new ideas step by step, check understanding often, and give pupils plenty of practice.

Areas of focus

  • English, Urdu and mathematics as daily core subjects
  • Science and social studies taught through enquiry and observation
  • Islamiyat, and ethics for students of other faiths where applicable
  • Art, physical education, library time and introductory computing

How children learn

Class teachers know each pupil well. Regular reading, neat written work and thoughtful homework build good study habits early.

Sample outline. Subjects and class structure will be confirmed by the school.

Stage three

Middle School

Greater depth, specialist subject teaching and the study skills students need for more demanding work.

Middle School bridges the primary and secondary years. Students meet subject teachers, handle a wider timetable and learn to organise their own work, with guidance close at hand.

Areas of focus

  • Deeper study in English, Urdu, mathematics and the sciences
  • History, geography and computing
  • Practical work, projects and presentations
  • Note-taking, revision and time management

How students learn

Lessons combine clear explanation with discussion and practical tasks. Form teachers follow each student's progress and wellbeing across subjects.

Sample outline. Subjects and class structure will be confirmed by the school.

Stage four

Secondary School

Focused preparation for board examinations, with guidance on subject choices and the steps that follow.

In the secondary years, students work towards their examinations with the support of experienced subject teachers. The emphasis is on thorough understanding, regular practice and steady, well-planned revision.

Areas of focus

  • Core and elective subjects in line with the school's examination pathway
  • Laboratory work in the sciences
  • Regular assessment with clear, practical feedback
  • Guidance on subject choices and further study

How students learn

Teachers set high expectations and help students meet them. Parents are kept informed through reports and meetings at key points in the year.

Sample outline. The examination board, subject options and class structure will be confirmed by the school.

Why choose our school

What families can expect from us

Choosing a school is a decision about the people who will help raise your child. These are the commitments that shape our daily work.

Thoughtful teaching

Well-planned lessons, clear explanations and regular checks for understanding, so no child is left guessing.

Personal attention

Teachers who know each pupil's strengths and difficulties, and who adapt their support accordingly.

Purposeful learning spaces

Orderly classrooms and shared areas arranged to help children concentrate, read, experiment and play.

Room for creativity

Art, drama, projects and problem-solving are woven into school life, so children learn to think and make as well as memorise.

Care for wellbeing

A kind, respectful atmosphere in which children feel safe, are listened to and learn to look after one another.

Open communication with parents

Regular updates, honest conversations about progress and a school office that is glad to hear from you.

Student life

Learning beyond the classroom

Confidence grows on the playing field, in the art room and on the stage as much as at a desk. We encourage every child to try something new each year.

Admissions

A simple enquiry journey

Joining a new school should feel straightforward. These four steps explain what happens after you get in touch.

  1. Send an enquiry

    Tell us a little about your child and the class you are interested in, using the enquiry form on this page.

  2. Speak with the school

    A member of our admissions team will answer your questions and explain the stage that suits your child.

  3. Arrange a visit

    Come and see the school, meet staff and get a feel for the classrooms and daily routine.

  4. Confirm the admission requirements

    We will explain the documents, any assessment and the next steps that apply to your child's class.

News and events

From around the school

Sample entries shown until the school publishes its own news

Sample entryEventDate to be confirmed

Annual Sports Day brings the whole school together

Races, team games and plenty of cheering from the sidelines, with every house and every age group taking part.

Sports Day is one of the most anticipated days in the school calendar. Students take part in track races, relays and team games, while the youngest children enjoy activity stations designed for their age.

The day is about effort and sportsmanship as much as winning. Parents are warmly invited to attend and cheer for every participant.

Sample entryReading

Reading Week: a book in every hand

Story sessions, book swaps and quiet reading across all classes.

During Reading Week, each class sets aside time every day for reading for pleasure. Older students read aloud to younger ones, classes exchange favourite titles, and teachers share the books that shaped their own childhoods.

Families are encouraged to read together at home for a few minutes each evening, in English, Urdu or any language spoken at home.

Sample entryScience

Young scientists present their projects

Models, experiments and explanations at the student science exhibition.

At the science exhibition, students work in small teams to investigate a question, build a model or demonstrate an experiment, and then explain their findings to visitors.

The exhibition gives students practice in planning, careful observation and speaking clearly about what they have learned.

Questions parents ask

Frequently asked questions

If your question is not answered here, please send us an enquiry and we will be happy to help.

Ask a question

How do I enquire about admission for my child?

Complete the enquiry form in the Contact section with your details, your child's current class and the stage you are interested in. The admissions team will then guide you through the next steps.

Can we visit the school before applying?

Yes, we encourage families to visit. Please mention in your enquiry that you would like to see the school, and we will arrange a suitable time with you.

Which classes and programmes does the school offer?

The Academics section describes four stages: Early Years, Primary School, Middle School and Secondary School. Please confirm with the school which classes are currently open for admission.

What are the admission requirements, fees and important dates?

Requirements vary by class, and fee and date information is shared directly by the school so that you always receive the current details. Send an enquiry and the admissions team will explain what applies to your child.

Is admission guaranteed once I send an enquiry?

An enquiry starts the conversation; it does not reserve a place. Admission depends on the availability of places in the relevant class and on completing the school's admission process.

What is the best way to contact the school?

Use the contact details and enquiry form in the Contact section below. Any phone number, email address or WhatsApp link listed there is the school's official channel.
